title: Monetary Policy and Economic Developments
summary: This is a historical Federal Reserve Monetary Policy Report reviewing U.S. monetary policy and economic developments in 2018, excerpted from reports published in February 2019 and July 2018. The FOMC raised the federal funds target range twice in H2 2018 to 2-1/4 to 2-1/2 percent, and signaled patience at its January 2019 meeting amid softer global conditions and muted inflation. Economic activity increased at a solid pace with unemployment near 4 percent and PCE inflation at 1.7 percent in December 2018.
key_points: FOMC raised target range for federal funds rate twice in H2 2018, ending at 2-1/4 to 2-1/2 percent following the December meeting
January 2019 FOMC meeting indicated the committee will be patient in determining future adjustments to support maximum employment and price stability
Payroll employment growth averaged 224,000 per month since June 2018; unemployment rate averaged just under 4 percent
PCE inflation declined to 1.7 percent in December 2018 from slightly above 2 percent in mid-2018, restrained by energy price declines; core PCE estimated at 1.9 percent
Real GDP increased at a solid rate in H2 2018 and rose a little under 3 percent for the full year
Financial conditions became less supportive of growth since July 2018, with risk appetite deteriorating amid trade tensions and global growth concerns
why_it_matters: This historical record documents the Fed's policy stance during 2018 when the tightening cycle was approaching its peak before the pivot to patience in early 2019. The report captures the transition from gradual rate increases to a more cautious approach as global conditions softened and inflation pressures moderated.
macro_context: The report describes a transition from robust growth in 2017 to a more uncertain outlook in late 2018. Foreign economic growth stepped down significantly, particularly in the euro area and China. Financial market volatility increased substantially in Q4 2018 with Treasury yields and equity prices declining. The Fed shifted from continued tightening to a patient stance signaling potential end to the rate-hike cycle.
